directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source contrasts the classical exp(-c(log x)^{1/10}) PNT error with the Vinogradov–Korobov exp(-c(log x)^{3/5}/(log log x)^{1/5}) error, notes qualitative uses of still stronger errors for smooth numbers, and compares both with the RH consequence O(sqrt(x)log²x). It states that wider-range power saving for zeta sums would widen the known zero-free region.
directed.conceptual_reading: The error term is interpreted as downstream evidence of the short-sum Fourier statement, while the cancellation range—not superficial similarity of error shapes—is the more informative structural invariant.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The zeta function transports Fourier-analytic cancellation of integer phases into zero locations and then into prime-counting error; the RH comparison supplies an external scale for the remaining gap.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The source explicitly offers no plausible route from the Vinogradov–Korobov method to the 1/2-line; improving its cancellation range would widen a near-one zero-free region but is not evidence of approaching RH.
